chunks: From him, from al-Haytham ibn Masrūq al-Nahdī, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said:
I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, and in his house there was a toilet facing the qiblah.

I heard him say: “Whoever urinates facing the qiblah, then remembers and turns away from it out of reverence for the qiblah and magnification of it, he will not rise from that seat of his before Allah forgives him.”

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction of prayer, treated here as a sacred orientation deserving reverence

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and spiritual significance of turning away from the qiblah while relieving oneself?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches reverence for the qiblah even in matters of personal cleanliness and bodily functions. It indicates that if a person realizes a mistake and turns away from the qiblah out of respect for it, Allah grants him forgiveness. The narration combines legal etiquette with spiritual awareness and veneration of sacred symbols.
